summary: All seven declared falsifications LAND. I applied each falsified_by mutation in a scratch copy of the tree, diffed to prove it landed, and in every case the row the field names went red with its paired control staying green: AC1 (STATUSES widened to admit load_bearing, 3 rows red including the named one, the status-unknown control green), AC2 (the recompute disabled, exactly 1 row red, the untouched-fixture control green), AC3 (the pin-level unrecognized-key refusal replaced with errs = 0, the three per-key rows plus the once-each cardinality row red), AC4 (disposition_for falling back to the settlement's own decided_by, 7 rows red including the forged-file negative control), AC5 (decided mapped onto load_bearing, the BLOCKED row and its companion red), AC6 (each protected_paths entry removed in turn, its own row red), AC7 (the is_dir stand-down guard deleted, exactly the recorded-stand-down row red). I also verified all four blockers the earlier review found are FIXED and not renamed: (1) AC7's declared falsification is corrected and the original is kept beside it - I confirmed independently on CPython 3.12.3 that Path('missing').glob('*.yaml') yields nothing and raises nothing, so the assertion the old field named truly could not fail; (2) all four closed key sets are now pinned by exact set equality - widening SCOPE_KEYS with modules_not_pinned and OBSERVATION_KEYS with verdict/ruled_by reds the AC3 set-equality row; (3) the live-emptiness pin is gone - I USED the feature, writing a real valid floor into .veldo/floors/, and the suite stayed 91 passed 0 failed and the full gate stayed GREEN; (4) floor_report's dropped unreadable floor is fixed with teeth - reverting it to a bare continue reds the named row. BUT the item's own reason to exist does not hold. Using only the organs this item ships and reads, I authored a complete ruling with NO human act: a floor, an accepted decision_choice request, and a settlement, all three written by me and none committed. floor_report then prints '1 ruled ... ruled incidental by an attributed human through request REQ-FORGE, bound to this observation's recomputed digest', while python3 .veldo/validate.py all exits 0, the suite is 91 passed 0 failed and bash scripts/verify.sh is GATE: GREEN. The floor half of the design is sound - I could not get a ruling into a pin - but the resolver's join runs through three fields nothing derives (the settlement's typed bound_digest, its chosen key, and a request_id it never binds back to the observation), and the protected-path control AC6 rests on cannot see an uncommitted file. Two further defects sit beside the criteria: the scope block's closed key set is only enforced when the floor declares pins, so a pins-less floor carrying exempt_paths and disposition validates with ZERO errors; and any file in .veldo/floors/ not named *.yaml is invisible to every reader, which is the confident zero the blocker-4 fix just closed for unparseable .yaml.

criteria.note: Drove the declared falsification: widened STATUSES from {"unknown"} to {"unknown", "load_bearing"} in .veldo/behavior_floor.py and its engine twin, proved it landed with git diff, and the suite went 88 passed 3 failed - including the row the field names ('a pin declaring status load_bearing is REFUSED by PIN_VOCAB_UNKNOWN, exactly once') and the exactly-one-member row. The paired NEGATIVE CONTROL ('the SAME validator accepts the SAME fixture with status unknown, printing nothing') stayed GREEN, so the refusal is discriminating and not a blanket rejection. Verified the rest of the criterion by reading the module and the rows that drive it: every PIN_REQUIRED field is refused by name when absent (six rows, one per field, each asserting the field name appears in the refusal), fidelity is the closed {exact, proxy} with both members accepted and a near-miss refused, a duplicate pin id is refused within one floor AND across the set naming both files, a floor with pins and no scope block is refused by SCOPE_MISSING, a scope block with no method is refused, a surface declared both enumerated and unreachable is refused, and a pin over a surface scope.enumerated does not declare is refused - that last one is the 'every internal reference resolves' leg and it is real. Verified the citations in the criterion by reading the lines: .veldo/decision.py:239-241 IS the duplicate-decision-id refusal. Everything is driven through the GATE WRAPPER (validate_checks.check_floors) over a temporary .veldo/floors/, not against a second copy of the module.

Drove the declared falsification: replaced the recompute guard in _validate_pin with `if False:` so observation.digest is accepted as declared, proved it landed, and the suite went 90 passed 1 failed - exactly the row the field names ('a pin whose observation.recorded was EDITED while its digest was left alone is refused by DIGEST_MISMATCH'), with the POSITIVE CONTROL (the untouched fixture accepted printing nothing) staying green. Verified the load-bearing property independently against the module: observation_digest is derived from OBSERVATION_DIGEST_FIELDS ('surface', 'recorded') only, it never reads the declared digest (I fed it a pin carrying digest sha256:0000000000000000 and got the same value back), it is a sorted-keys json.dumps plus one hash exactly as request.request_digest at .veldo/request.py:126-136 over DIGEST_FIELDS at :113-114 (both verified by reading), and BOTH the validator and disposition_for call the one function. Also confirmed there is no path by which the digest check is skipped while the pin is still accepted: a missing or non-string recorded or digest fires PIN_FIELD_MISSING, so errs is never zero when the recompute is not reached. TWO LIMITS on the criterion's strength, filed as F5 and F6. The tuple excludes fidelity and reproduces, so a granted ruling survives the machine flipping exact to proxy and re-pointing the reproducing test (driven), and the digest is sha256 truncated to 16 hex characters, so 'can never silently rule the other' rests on 64 bits.

The declared falsification lands and the PIN-level closure is airtight, but the criterion's own two sentences are FALSE for a floor that declares no pins, and nothing in the suite drives that case. Driven falsification first: replaced `errs = _unknown_keys(pin, PIN_KEYS, ...)` with `errs = 0` in _validate_pin, proved it landed, and the suite went 87 passed 4 failed - the three per-key rows (decided_by, reason, exempt_paths) plus the 'refused ONCE EACH and nothing else fires' cardinality row, with the no-planted-keys control green. I also verified the earlier review's blocker-2 fix has real teeth: widening SCOPE_KEYS with modules_not_pinned and OBSERVATION_KEYS with verdict and ruled_by reds the exact-set-equality row (90 passed 1 failed), so the closed sets are pinned by enumeration and not by a word blacklist. THE REFUTATION: validate_floor returns EARLY when pins is empty or absent (`if not pins: _standdown(...); return errs`), and _validate_scope is called AFTER that return. So a floor whose scope block carries waived_paths: legacy/**, modules_not_pinned: billing, ruled_by: dmitry and disposition: incidental, with no pins, validates with ZERO errors, stands down as 'the floor declares no pins', and leaves the suite at 91 passed 0 failed. That falsifies 'disposition ... structurally unwriteable inside a floor rather than merely discouraged' and 'no path, glob, module or pattern scoped exemption is representable', and it falsifies the module docstring's 'Every key set is CLOSED (the floor, its scope block, each pin, each observation)'. The floor-level key set IS checked before the early return, so only the scope and pin levels are affected. Filed as F3 with a one-line fix. Separately, and disclosed honestly by the suite's own row but not by the spec: `surface` is unconstrained free text, so a pin whose surface is `legacy/**` is representable and the spec text was never narrowed to match the suite's.

The resolver implements exactly the conditions the criterion declares, and the declared falsification lands hard - but every one of those conditions is machine-writable, so the criterion's headline ('A RULING IS RESOLVED ONLY FROM A DECISION THAT WENT THROUGH THE TICKET CHANNEL') does not hold in practice. Driven falsification: made disposition_for fall back to the settlement's own decided_by when _accepted_request returns None, proved it landed, and the suite went 84 passed 7 failed - the named NEGATIVE CONTROL ('a hand-written settlement carrying the pin's RIGHT digest with NO accepted veldo.request/v1 record behind it rules NOTHING'), all five request-shape rows (no request, open, rejected, wrong touchpoint, id mismatch), and the filesystem leg. The POSITIVE CONTROL stayed green. Verified the rest independently: the join is one-directional and no key in FLOOR_KEYS, SCOPE_KEYS, PIN_KEYS or OBSERVATION_KEYS names a request, settlement, decision or ticket; mutating recorded or surface changes the digest so the same settlement stops matching; the resolver really does read .veldo/settlements/*.json and .veldo/requests/*.yaml from disk; and the cited lines are real (.veldo/request.py:74-77 TOUCHPOINTS, :273-274 the accepted-binding rule, .veldo/request_reconcile.py's settlement writer). THE RESIDUAL, filed as F1 and driven end to end: _accepted_request checks only schema, id, touchpoint and status, and NEVER compares the request's own bound_artifact.digest to the pin's recomputed digest, while the settlement's bound_digest is a TYPED field and `chosen` is read at face value. So a settlement naming ANY accepted decision_choice request rules ANY observation. The criterion's own argument condemns its own mechanism ('a digest that is merely typed is a writable pointer at somebody else's judgement'), and its closing generalization 'so a forged file is not a ruling' is true only of the single forgery it tests.

Drove the declared falsification: mapped the settlement word decided onto load_bearing when no chosen option is present, proved it landed, and the suite went 86 passed 5 failed - the named BLOCKED/RULING_NOT_CARRIED row, its COMPANION ('a blocked pin is NEVER reported as ruled and NEVER silently reported as unknown'), the shipped-inbound-edge row and both report rows. Verified the premise independently rather than taking the quotation: the suite loads the REAL .veldo/request_reconcile.py and drives _settlement_record for a decision_choice acceptance, and I confirmed by reading the source that bound_digest is the request's bound_artifact.digest and that no chosen key is written, so BLOCKED is what today's channel produces and not an unreachable state. Verified RULING_NOT_SETTLED and RULING_NOT_CARRIED are different names, never collapse, and that a chosen option outside RULINGS blocks rather than being taken at face value. The report carries pins/ruled/unknown/blocked BESIDE enumerated_surfaces and unreachable_surfaces, has no ratio key and no float, names the unanalyzed languages, and prints one line per pin with its reason. I ALSO VERIFIED THE EARLIER REVIEW'S BLOCKER 4: reverting the unreadable-floor handling to a bare `continue` reds 'A FLOOR THAT COULD NOT BE READ IS COUNTED AND NAMED' (90 passed 1 failed), so that fix has teeth. ONE OVERCLAIM the criterion's own framing rests on, folded into F1: the spec says 'Until it lands, every pin reads unknown or blocked, which is the honest reading'. That is false about the code - the resolver reads a top-level `chosen` key at face value, and since AC5's own row proves the shipped edge never writes one, the ONLY reachable path to `ruled` today is a settlement no shipped writer can produce.

Drove BOTH declared falsifications through the live policy: deleting the .veldo/floors/* line from .veldo/policy.yaml reds exactly the floors row (90 passed 1 failed), deleting the .veldo/settlements/* line reds exactly the settlement row. Both assertions go through policy_check.protected_patterns() plus the two fnmatch forms policy_check.py:439-447 actually uses, so they pin the mechanism and not a string in a document - I read that enforcement block to confirm the forms match. The NEGATIVE CONTROL is real: .veldo/behavior_floor.py and the spec file match no protected pattern while .veldo/policy.yaml does. Verified the engine twin carries both registrations as text and that policy.yaml is a DECLARED exception to the byte-identical template sync (scripts/check_template_sync.sh:33 returns 0 for it, read directly). Verified the human act exists: proof/VELDO-0012/approval-dmitry.json is present, which is more than the sibling item at the same commit carries. THE GAP, filed as F2 and driven: the enforcement runs over policy_check.changed_files(), which is `git diff --name-only <base>` and therefore never lists UNTRACKED files, while disposition_for and floor_report read the working tree. With a floor, a request and a settlement sitting untracked in .veldo/, changed_files() returned 0 files and the full gate was GREEN. So 'adding a floor, re-pointing an observation, or writing a settlement is a change that needs a commit-bound, path-scoped approval, so the agent being gated cannot author the record that exempts it' holds only for a COMMITTED record. The blind spot is in policy_check.py, which this item does not touch and which has it for .veldo/secret_inventory.json too, so I have scored the registration itself confirmed.

Drove the CORRECTED falsification: deleted the `if not d.is_dir()` stand-down from check_floors_dir, proved it landed, and the suite went 90 passed 1 failed - exactly the recorded-stand-down row the corrected field names, and NOT the byte-identity row. I verified the correction's own claim rather than trusting it: on CPython 3.12.3 Path('/nonexistent-xyz').glob('*.yaml') returns [] and raises nothing, so the assertion the ORIGINAL field named was structurally incapable of failing, exactly as recorded. VERIFIED THE EARLIER REVIEW'S BLOCKER 3 BY USING THE FEATURE: I wrote a real, valid one-pin floor into .veldo/floors/ in the scratch copy; validate.py all exited 0, the suite stayed 91 passed 0 failed, and bash scripts/verify.sh printed GATE: GREEN. The stand-down rows now drive over a temporary path that cannot exist and the live row reports the state it measured instead of requiring emptiness, so no assertion pins today's empty floors directory. Re-derived the AC7 domain myself from scripts/verify.sh rather than reading the row's claim: 8 required catalog items, 12 stage paths, a transitive closure of 32 files with every member on disk, strictly larger than the stage set, and containing .veldo/validate_checks.py and .veldo/behavior_floor.py. Confirmed repo-wide with grep that disposition_for appears as an IDENTIFIER only in behavior_floor.py and its engine twin (every other hit is prose in a docstring or the spec), so no gate stage reads a disposition and none can refuse on one. Confirmed the registration is real at .veldo/validate.py:832 (`check_decisions() + _VC.check_floors()`), that /veldo:init lays the organ down (.veldo/init_scaffold.py:72 and :143), and that both the organ and the wrapper are byte-identical to their engine twins. NOTE on the domain, not a defect: the closure excludes .veldo/policy_check.py and scripts/veldo-guard.sh because they are not verify.sh stages, which is what the criterion's own definition of the domain produces.

findings.text: A `ruled` disposition is reachable with NO human act, using only files the machine can author. disposition_for resolves a ruling from three fields nothing derives: the settlement's bound_digest (a TYPED field, never recomputed from anything), the settlement's `chosen` key (read at face value), and a request_id that _accepted_request checks only for schema, id, touchpoint and status - it NEVER compares the request's own bound_artifact.digest to the pin's recomputed observation digest, even though the shipped receipt path sets bound_digest FROM that exact field (.veldo/request_reconcile.py:451, `displayed = (record.get('bound_artifact') or {}).get('digest')`), so the comparison is free. Two consequences. (a) FORGERY: writing .veldo/settlements/x.json and .veldo/requests/x.yaml by hand produces a ruling, and the reason string asserts a binding nobody verified: 'ruled incidental by an attributed human through request REQ-FORGE, bound to this observation's recomputed digest'. No attribution is read: the settled_by, decided_by and approvers fields are present in the record and consulted by nothing, and the append-only compare-and-swap receipt and the attributed changelog the spec's Context section credits for the actor are never touched by this reader. (b) TRANSFER, which is the harm the item exists to prevent: because the request is never bound back to the observation, a settlement can name a REAL accepted decision_choice request that a human settled about a DIFFERENT artifact, and it rules this pin. This falsifies the spec title's 'the ruling is representable ONLY as a human decision settled through the ticket channel', AC4's 'a forged file is not a ruling', and the Context claim 'Until it lands, every pin reads unknown or blocked' - the resolver accepts a `chosen` key that AC5's own row proves the shipped edge never writes, so today the ONLY reachable route to `ruled` is a record no shipped writer can produce. MITIGATION, stated so this can be weighed: nothing consumes disposition_for yet (AC7, which I verified), and committing these records would need a path-scoped approval - though the reviewer of a settlement diff has no signal that the request cited was about something else. FIX: compare the accepted request's bound_artifact.digest to the recomputed observation digest, and refuse (not silently accept) a settlement carrying an option the channel cannot yet carry.
findings.evidence: In /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dmitry-projects-myday/44b01d2e-70df-4b27-8687-62188cce6732/scratchpad/rev-VELDO-0012 I wrote three files I authored myself and committed none: .veldo/floors/billing.yaml (one valid pin, status unknown, digest sha256:95f4a55a00323924 computed by the module), .veldo/requests/REQ-FORGE.yaml (schema veldo.request/v1, touchpoint decision_choice, status accepted, request_hash computed with request.request_digest, bound_artifact.digest the pin digest) and .veldo/settlements/REQ-FORGE-c1.json (schema veldo.decision/v1, decision decided, bound_digest the pin digest, chosen incidental). Then: `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` -> exit 0; `validate_checks.check_floors()` -> 0 errors; `behavior_floor.report_lines(floor_report(...))` -> 'behaviour floor: 1 floor(s), 1 pin(s): 1 ruled, 0 unknown, 0 blocked' and '  billing.yaml PIN-1: ruled - ruled incidental by an attributed human through request REQ-FORGE, bound to this observation's recomputed digest'; `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 18_veldo_0012_behaviour_floor_contract` -> 91 passed, 0 failed; `bash scripts/verify.sh` -> exit 0, 'GATE: GREEN (dda45bff3e86fb336f5899f37ed6678a42ce06b6)'. The transfer leg driven separately with injected records: a settlement carrying bound_digest = a pin's digest and request_id REQ-REAL-7, against an accepted decision_choice request whose bound_artifact.digest was sha256:deadbeefdeadbeef, returned {'disposition': 'ruled', 'ruling': 'incidental', 'request': 'REQ-REAL-7'}.

findings.text: The protected-path control AC6 rests on cannot see an uncommitted record, and every reader in this item reads the working tree. policy_check.changed_files() is `git diff --name-only <base>` (.veldo/policy_check.py:92-99), which reports modifications to TRACKED files and never lists untracked ones, and the protected-path block at :439-447 iterates exactly that set. behavior_floor._load_settlements, _load_requests and floor_report read the filesystem directly. So an agent that writes .veldo/floors/x.yaml and .veldo/settlements/y.json and simply does not commit them gets the full effect with no approval demanded, no gate refusal, and nothing recorded. AC6's sentence 'adding a floor, re-pointing an observation, or writing a settlement is a change that needs a commit-bound, path-scoped approval, so the agent being gated cannot author the record that exempts it' is therefore true only of committed records. This is not a defect this item introduced - the same blind spot applies to .veldo/secret_inventory.json, which AC6 cites as its precedent - but it is the load-bearing half of this item's answer to 'the validator is not the integrity', and the artifact it protects is one a local consumer reads from disk. Any later item that makes a precondition out of a disposition (item 4 in the spec's own Notes) inherits a control that a local run bypasses by not staging a file. FIX direction: the consumer of a disposition should require the record to be TRACKED and covered by an approval, rather than merely present.
findings.evidence: In the scratch copy at HEAD I created .veldo/floors/smuggled.yaml and .veldo/settlements/forged.json, then: `git status --short` -> '?? .veldo/floors/' and '?? .veldo/settlements/'; `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 | grep -c 'floors\|settlements'` -> 0; and policy_check loaded in-process reported `changed_files()` count 0 with no floors/settlements member, while `protected_patterns()` correctly ends with ['.veldo/floors/*', '.veldo/settlements/*']. With the full forged chain of F1 present and untracked, `bash scripts/verify.sh` was GATE: GREEN.

findings.text: The scope block's closed key set is only enforced when the floor declares pins, so an exemption IS representable in a floor the gate accepts. validate_floor checks the FLOOR-level key set, then hits `if not pins: _standdown(...); return errs` and returns BEFORE _validate_scope is ever called (.veldo/behavior_floor.py:402-411). A floor with a scope block and no pins therefore has its scope keys unchecked. I wrote .veldo/floors/exemption.yaml carrying scope.waived_paths: legacy/**, scope.modules_not_pinned: billing, scope.ruled_by: dmitry and scope.disposition: incidental, with no pins: check_floors() returned 0 errors, validate.py all exited 0, and the VELDO-0012 suite stayed 91 passed 0 failed. That falsifies AC3's 'NO RULING AND NO EXEMPTION IS REPRESENTABLE IN THE FLOOR AT ALL', its 'disposition ... structurally unwriteable inside a floor rather than merely discouraged', its 'no path, glob, module or pattern scoped exemption is representable', and the module docstring's 'Every key set is CLOSED (the floor, its scope block, each pin, each observation)'. It is the same defect class as the blocker the earlier review found one level up: the enumeration was fixed, the CALL SITE is conditional. The suite cannot see it because every AC3 scope row builds its fixture with `_bf_floor([_bf_pin()], scope={...})`, i.e. always with a pin. Mitigating: with no pins there is no observation, so nothing can attach a ruling to it and the file is inert - but the criterion's claim is about representability, and a gate-green floor that literally reads `waived_paths: legacy/**` is the artifact the design exists to make impossible, and the reviewer of that diff is exactly the reader this design says must not be relied on for semantics. FIX, one line: validate the scope block whenever it is present, before the pins early return (and keep the pins-less stand-down).
findings.evidence: Scratch copy at HEAD, .veldo/floors/exemption.yaml as described: `validate_checks.check_floors()` -> 0; `behavior_floor.floor_standdowns()` -> one entry, 'the floor declares no pins, so there is nothing to validate and nothing to read a disposition for'; `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` -> exit 0; `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 18_veldo_0012_behaviour_floor_contract` -> 91 passed, 0 failed. Contrast: the same scope keys in a floor WITH one pin are correctly refused by PIN_KEY_UNRECOGNIZED, which is what the suite's AC3 rows drive.

findings.text: A file in .veldo/floors/ that is not named *.yaml is invisible to every reader, and the report states a confident zero over it. check_floors_dir and floor_report both iterate `d.glob("*.yaml")`, so a floor written as contracts.yml is not validated, not counted, not named as unreadable, and not reported. I put a contracts.yml in .veldo/floors/ carrying status: load_bearing, decided_by: dmitry, reason: 'the whole legacy tree is incidental, signed off', exempt_paths: legacy/** and surface: legacy/** - every single thing AC1 and AC3 exist to refuse - and validate.py all exited 0 while report_lines printed 'behaviour floor: stood down - no floor in .veldo/floors/ declares a pin, so there is no recorded behaviour to read a disposition for'. That is a confident zero: the input was never recorded. It is also the exact defect the earlier review's blocker 4 closed for an unparseable .yaml ('a bare continue here would quote a coverage figure computed over the floors that happened to parse - which is the one thing this report must not do'), reachable one extension away, and it falsifies the module docstring's 'FAIL CLOSED. The moment a floor exists, anything malformed refuses by NAME'. AC1 does declare the record shape as .veldo/floors/*.yaml, so a .yml file is arguably not a floor - but the directory is a PROTECTED path whose whole purpose is that its contents are reviewed, and a human reading that directory sees a signed-off exemption that the machine reports as absent. FIX: name every file in the floors directory that the *.yaml rule does not claim, in the report and in the check, rather than skipping it.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy at HEAD with .veldo/floors/contracts.yml as described and no other floor: `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` -> exit 0; floor_report(parse=...) -> standdown True, reason 'no floor in .veldo/floors/ declares a pin...', pins 0, unreadable []; report_lines -> the single stood-down line. `ls .veldo/floors/` -> contracts.yml.

findings.text: OBSERVATION_DIGEST_FIELDS is ('surface', 'recorded'), so fidelity and reproduces sit OUTSIDE the join and a granted ruling survives their rewrite. After a human rules load_bearing on a pin whose fidelity is exact and whose reproduces names tests/test_billing.py::test_cap, the machine can flip fidelity to proxy and re-point reproduces at a test that asserts nothing, and disposition_for still returns ruled load_bearing on the same digest. The suite asserts this exclusion as CORRECT, so it is a deliberate choice and not an oversight - but two claims built on it are false about the code. The spec's Notes say of the reproduces reference 'the digest is what makes the reference load bearing rather than decorative': it is not, the digest does not cover it, and a pin can point at any test. And the spec's own open decision reserves for later whether 'a proxy pin may ever be the load-bearing guard that blocks a change', a distinction the machine can erase after the ruling without changing the digest. If a later item consumes fidelity or reproduces, the human's judgement will already be attached to a claim they did not make.
findings.evidence: Driven against the shipped module in the scratch copy: a pin with fidelity exact and reproduces tests/test_billing.py::test_cap resolved to ruled/load_bearing against a settlement and accepted request; the same pin with fidelity proxy and reproduces tests/test_nothing.py::test_always_passes produced an IDENTICAL digest (True) and resolved to ruled/load_bearing from the same settlement.

findings.text: The one join between a human's ruling and a behaviour is sha256 truncated to 16 hex characters, i.e. 64 bits ('sha256:' + hexdigest()[:16], .veldo/behavior_floor.py:261). AC2 claims two pins recording a byte-identical observation on two different surfaces get different digests 'so one human's judgement about one of them can never silently rule the other'. Moving a ruling onto an EXISTING digest is a second preimage at 2^64 and not a practical concern, but the drafting pass authors both pins, and a birthday collision between two observations chosen at drafting time is about 2^32 hashes over short inputs - hours of ordinary CPU, not a research result. The consequence is precisely the transfer the surface-in-the-tuple exists to prevent: two pins, one innocuous and one load bearing, sharing a digest, so a human ruling incidental on the first also rules the second. This is the repository's established convention (request.request_digest truncates identically), so it is not a novel decision here and the fix is repo-wide rather than local - but 'can never' is stronger than 64 bits, and a floor's digest is the one hash in this repository whose collision grants an exemption. NOT DRIVEN: I did not run a collision search, so this is arithmetic over the truncation I did verify by reading and by running the function.
findings.evidence: behavior_floor.observation_digest returns values matching ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{16}$ (e.g. sha256:95f4a55a00323924 for the pin used in F1), from `hashlib.sha256(blob.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]` at .veldo/behavior_floor.py:261; .veldo/request.py:136 is the identical truncation.

findings.text: The proof bundle records no driven falsification. proof/VELDO-0012/ holds manifest.json and approval-dmitry.json only, while most bundles in this same commit carry a driven-falsifications.txt. All seven of the manifest's criteria carry the SAME single evidence string - 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 91 passed, 0 failed in 0.56s' - so the producer's seven passed claims rest on the suite being green, which is the one thing VELDO-0001 exists to say is not proof: a green check is not evidence the check can fail. The runner prints 'PARTIAL RUN: no proof manifest, no evidence claim and no landing decision may cite this' on that exact invocation, and the manifest cites it seven times. The manifest also names commit e4ce85da95291b0ec50eb22384132306bbddfddd while HEAD is dda45bff3e86fb336f5899f37ed6678a42ce06b6, so the bundle is one commit behind the tree it describes. I drove all seven falsifications myself and all seven land, so the property holds - what is missing is the record.
findings.evidence: `ls -la proof/VELDO-0012/` -> approval-dmitry.json, manifest.json. `cat proof/VELDO-0012/manifest.json` -> commit e4ce85da9529, and seven criteria each with the identical unit evidence ref. `git -C /home/dmitry/projects/veldo rev-parse HEAD` -> dda45bff3e86fb336f5899f37ed6678a42ce06b6. `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 18_veldo_0012_behaviour_floor_contract` prints the PARTIAL RUN warning after the summary line the manifest quotes.
